topic: NextAuth.js v5 / Auth.js: Authentication for Next.js AI Applications

competitors.title: Migrating to v5 - Auth.js Official Documentation
key_points: NextAuth.js v5 is a major rewrite with native App Router support; configuration moves from pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts to a root-level auth.ts file
New auth() function replaces getServerSession() across Server Components, Route Handlers, API Routes, and middleware — no arguments needed
Environment variables renamed: NEXTAUTH_SECRET → AUTH_SECRET, AUTH_URL auto-detected from headers
All env vars should be prefixed with AUTH_; provider secrets auto-detected (e.g., AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET)
Adapters moved from @next-auth/* to @auth/* namespace (e.g., @auth/prisma-adapter)
Edge compatibility achieved via two-file split: auth.config.ts (edge-safe, no adapter) + auth.ts (full config with adapter)
No breaking changes to database schema from v4; OAuth 1.0 support dropped
NextAuthOptions renamed to NextAuthConfig; types re-exported from framework packages

competitors.title: Next.js Authentication with Auth.js (NextAuth v5) (2026) — Techoral
key_points: Complete setup guide including auth.ts configuration, route handler, OAuth providers (GitHub, Google), Credentials provider with Zod validation
JWT vs Database sessions explained: JWT = faster per-request, no DB dependency but session invalidation requires waiting for expiry
Database sessions = immediate revocability but one extra DB query per authenticated request
RBAC via JWT callbacks: persist role to token in jwt() callback, expose on session via session() callback
Middleware route protection using auth() wrapper with matcher pattern to skip static files
Custom login pages via pages config option (signIn, error, verifyRequest)
Server Actions for sign-in/sign-out using 'use server' directive with imported signIn/signOut functions

competitors.title: Auth.js v5 with Next.js 16: The Complete Authentication Guide (2026) — DEV Community
key_points: v5 brings: native App Router support, better TypeScript types, Edge runtime compatibility, simpler configuration, built-in CSRF protection
Route handler is just 2 lines: export const { GET, POST } = handlers; from @/lib/auth
Server Component protection: const session = await auth(); if (!session?.user) redirect('/login')
API route protection: call auth() at top of handler, return 401 if no session
Common mistakes: using getServerSession from v4, forgetting route handler, not extending types for custom fields
TypeScript module augmentation needed for custom session fields (like role) via next-auth.d.ts
Prisma schema requirements: User model with accounts, sessions relations; Role enum pattern

competitors.title: Next.js Auth With NextAuth.js v5: Complete 2026 Setup Guide — Rajesh R Nair
key_points: Breaking changes detailed: config file location, auth() replaces getServerSession, adapter package renames, env variable renames
Database sessions with Prisma and PostgreSQL: specific schema models (User, Account, Session, VerificationToken)
JWT vs Database deep dive: JWT sessions encrypt data into cookie — cannot invalidate specific sessions until expiry
Database sessions ideal for B2B/enterprise where admins may need to force-logout compromised accounts
Middleware matcher pattern critical: must skip static files (_next, images, fonts) or performance degrades significantly
Complete Prisma schema with all required models for full Auth.js adapter compatibility

competitors.title: NextAuth to Auth.js Migration Guide: Fixing Every Breaking Change in 2026 — Web3 AI Blog
key_points: Migration takes ~half a day of mechanical edits plus a day of testing; 2 days if custom adapter logic
Two-file split (auth.config.ts + auth.ts) is critical for Edge runtime compatibility
auth.config.ts used by middleware (edge-safe, no Node deps); auth.ts imported by Server Components with adapter
withAuth middleware wrapper is gone; replaced by auth() wrapper with custom callback logic
Google provider: v5 requires explicit scope declaration (profile email openid)
Drizzle adapter has largest schema delta from v4; check reference schema before migrating
Redirect-loop trap: ensure middleware matcher excludes auth pages or check path explicitly
